240	All of this is forbidden. "It shall not be" — and so it is written: orlah is
241	forbidden for three years.
242	If someone wants to make the blessing of the flowering trees on it, since
243	he does not yet see fruit, there are those who prevent it,
244	who say it is not good. But in terms of the law, it is truly permitted.
245	There is no need to be stringent about orlah. Orlah is nature,
246	the nature of the world: every tree must wait three
247	years, and afterward it is permitted to you to eat. So this is
248	not like something HaShem finds unpleasant, it is not
249	like kilayim, which the Torah forbade. Here
250	every tree, in its natural way, must pass three
251	years, the first ones.
252	Therefore it is permitted
253	to bless on an orlah tree, even though three
254	years are not yet complete and it is still forbidden to eat from it,
255	nevertheless.
256	Let us now return to the matters of Pesach.
257	We ask about the laws of Pesach thirty days before Pesach.
258	The Peri Chadash writes that even on Purim itself is already one
259	of the thirty days.
260	Now we are within the thirty days, Purim has passed
261	and the day after it too, so how much remains is less
262	than thirty. HaShem, within thirty days before Pesach,
263	atones for the sins of Israel. So writes Rabbi Chaim,
264	in the name of
265	the Chesed LeAvraham. He writes that HaShem
266	forgives His people Israel: each night, one thirtieth
267	of their sins is waived for them, a thirtieth part,
268	until they reach Pesach clean, like
269	Yom Kippur, completely clean of every sin, of every transgression.
270	Yes, this is a great merit: every evening HaShem
271	forgives us. Therefore
272	we ask about the laws of Pesach; also the Torah study we
273	do on the laws of Pesach helps as well,
274	to bring about this help. HaShem commanded this,
275	and He forgives us all our sins.
276	Now, as for why we must study
277	thirty days, we learned this from Moshe Rabbeinu. Moshe Rabbeinu,
278	when Israel made
279	Pesach in the second year after leaving Egypt, not in the
280	first year, in the second year, as written in Parashat Behaalotecha.
281	HaShem said to Moshe: "Let the children of Israel make
282	the Pesach in its appointed time." He commanded them to make
283	the Pesach, and so it was, and they made the Pesach.
284	"And there were men who were impure through contact with a human corpse, and they could not
285	make the Pesach on that day." Who were they?
286	Mishael and Eltzafan, those who carried the bodies of Nadav and Avihu,
287	as Moshe Rabbeinu had commanded, who died when Nadav and Avihu, fire went out
288	from before HaShem. They had offered a incense which HaShem had not
289	commanded them. The incense must
290	come from the community,
291	where every Jew contributes a half-shekel
292	in the month of Adar. With this money they buy the incense, this is
293	a communal offering. But they took and made, like the model of
294	the incense, and offered it. They placed it on the golden altar. They
295	were not wicked to do so. Whoever makes
296	an incense like this, an individual's incense,
297	it is called strange incense, as it is written, "and they offered
298	before HaShem strange fire, which He had not commanded them." Then fire went out
299	from HaShem and consumed them. Not that they were actually burned.
300	Two sparks of fire came out, like two flames, and each
301	one entered into one nostril.
302	They entered like this, and immediately
303	they fainted and died on the spot.
304	So the poor ones remained, one next to the other, lying.
305	Moshe Rabbeinu called Mishael
306	and Eltzafan and said to them: "Draw near, carry your brothers from before the
307	sanctuary." A dead body cannot be brought into the
308	Temple, so they took them out outside. "And they drew near and carried them"
309	in their tunics.
310	…
311	He said: "Your brothers, the whole house of Israel, will weep over the burning that
312	HaShem kindled." For they were great sages and great
313	tzaddikim, but they stumbled in this matter. They thought they were doing
314	the will of HaShem, and red flames of fire
315	went out and entered their nostrils, and so they died.
316	Therefore they became impure: when they carried them and took them out
317	outside, they touched the dead.
318	So they became impure.
319	Therefore these could not make the Pesach offering, the Pesach offering,
320	and eat it in purity, in holiness, not in impurity, and they were
321	already impure. What to do? So what does Moshe
322	Rabbeinu do? "Why should we be diminished, not offering the Pesach offering?" All
323	of us, the house of Israel, are fulfilling the mitzvah of
324	HaShem, and we cause that, because we did a mitzvah,
325	we took them out of the Sanctuary, we should
326	lose the mitzvah of Pesach?
327	So he said: "Stand, and I will hear what HaShem commands concerning you." And HaShem
328	commanded him: "Any man who is impure through a dead body,"
329	yes, "and wants to make the Pesach, let him make the Pesach in the
330	second month," not in Nissan, which is the first month,
331	but on the fourteenth of Iyar.
332	And then he makes the Pesach offering. Therefore, in remembrance of that
333	day, we do not say Vidui on the fourteenth of Iyar.
334	It is like Pesach: we do not say Vidui, we do not say
335	Tachanun, "Nefilat Apayim." It is a wonder
336	that it is considered like a Yom Tov, even though now we have no
337	Temple and no Pesach offering, but a remembrance remains
338	for us. The fourteenth of Iyar is the day on which the
339	Pesach Sheni offering is brought: whoever was impure and did not make the first Pesach
340	makes the second Pesach.
341	Therefore on that day we do as on Yom Tov:
342	we say no Vidui and no Nefilat Apayim.
343	And Moshe Rabbeinu, when they asked him, answered them what
344	HaShem had said: that they should not make the Pesach now with
345	all of Israel, but they have a make-up date, another thirty days.
346	That was enough; he had answered their question.
347	Yes, but he continued to speak: "They shall leave none of it until
348	morning,
349	and a bone they shall not break in it; according to all the statute of Pesach they shall make
350	it." Why was it necessary to add things? They asked
351	you, "Shall we make Pesach? Why should we be diminished?" Tell them, yes,
352	it is diminished. HaShem commands that you not make the first
353	Pesach now, make the second Pesach. Why was it necessary
354	to detail for them all the laws of Pesach? It is written: "They shall not
355	leave of it until morning, and a bone they shall not break in it.
356	According to all the statute of Pesach they shall make it." Why was it necessary to elaborate?
357	Because Moshe is standing at the first Pesach and tells them
358	the laws of the second Pesach, which is after thirty days. And here
